column1: # Torsion measured on whole strings (README.md, "Measured torsion"). A section measured string's optional
# `torsion-measured ID` record selects one row; the string must be the row's specimen (pack and line-density
# property) at the row's speaking length. Only the open string: a stop profile refuses. No other string is measured.

column8: Mansour, Woodhouse & Scavone 2016, Enhanced wave-based modelling of musical strings, Part 2: Bowed strings (Acta Acustica united with Acustica, companion to Part 1; author manuscript of 12 September 2016), section 2.2: "For the open cello D3 string studied here the torsional fundamental frequency is taken to be 758 Hz, the characteristic torsional impedance is 1.8 kg/s and a constant Q of 34 is assigned to all torsional modes." Part 2 names neither the string's make nor its length; it is bound here to the companion Part 1's cello D3, the D'Addario Kaplan Solutions D3 at 0.69 m, on the reading that both parts model the same string. Q 34 is the average that Woodhouse & Loach (Torsional behaviour of cello strings, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 85(5):734-740, 1999) measured over the first few torsional modes of steel-cored cello strings, almost constant over those modes; applying it to every mode is Mansour's assignment. The impedance is sqrt(K_R I_R)/r^2.
